usd_note: 'llm.*.usd' was computed in the container at $0.75/$3.75 per M (the price OpenRouter billed in our 3 Nov probe); 'usd_at_harness_price' re-prices the same logged tokens at evaluate.PRICE_USD ($0.825/$4.125), the price every wiki and RAG query cost in the lecture uses.
timing_note: The build container was pre-empted by Modal after the READ pass (log: logs/wiki_build_modal_stdout.txt) and restarted with the same input; the restart replayed all 1,068 READ calls from the cassette, so seconds.read (132.6 s) is replay time. The first attempt's READ, live, ran from about 10:51:27 to between 10:57:53 and 10:58:53 IST for its first 1,000 of 1,067 parts (40 parallel workers): about 7 minutes. WRITE (186.6 s), merge and parse are live timings from the restart. Live build wall time is therefore about 7.5 + 0.6 + 3.1 = 11 minutes.

design.reader: wiki_sources.py: same extraction as eval/check_gold.py (pypdf, OCR for scans, python-docx, openpyxl, csv, email, html), so page numbers match the golden set. corpus.py (the RAG parser) is used at query time for raw-source look-ups (open_source), which gives exact sheet/row and page locations.
design.units: one READ call per source part: PDFs in parts of about 18,000 characters with [p. N] markers (8,000 for the dense error, screen and service references); every other file whole unless long.
design.structured_data: masters and extracts are never copied: each sheet is shown as a profile (title rows, columns, row count, per-column fill/distinct/examples) plus all rows when the sheet has 60 rows or fewer, else the first 5 rows and only the rows whose key appears in the prose documents (entities that get pages), 60 rows per part. Printed registers (06_transactions/reports) are read from their first 2 pages. Result: 27 data-source pages that say what each file holds and how to look a row up; table look-ups at query time open the raw sheet row.
design.registry: the page namespace is seeded by code from Northbridge's own codes (document codes, user ids, supplier codes named in the prose, cost centres, roles, screens, service groups, item prefixes): 480 slugs. Each READ call gets the document/data/role slugs plus only the entities its text names, so prompts stay about 10k tokens.
design.map_reduce: batch ingest = READ (map: facts per page, with a verbatim quote and location, checked by code) -> MERGE (code canonicalisation + one LLM call to merge near-duplicate new slugs) -> WRITE (reduce: one call per page from all its facts; References generated by code from the facts' locations) -> index.md, lists/, log.md by code. log.md replays each source's contribution in ingest order. update() is the true incremental path.
design.permissions: facts from 01_policies/HR/CONFIDENTIAL go only to HR pages (audience hr, restricted/, restricted/index.md); staff pages citing HR files: 0 (lint).
design.index: index.md lists every document, topic, decision, supplier, role and data-source page; the 7 big code-named families (screens, service groups, error codes, error lists, item families, people, cost centres) get one line with the slug rule and a link to lists/list-<type>.md, like Wikipedia list pages. Summaries cut to 110 characters. This was rebuilt by code (reindex) after the first queries showed a 126 KB, ~32k-token index.
